case_policy: This candidate audits a deliberately scoped two-electrode parity model. It does not claim that every EIS equivalent circuit is non-identifiable or that the source authors overclaimed their results.

claims.title: Linear full-cell EIS alone uniquely allocates electrode contributions
claims.claim_text: Within the declared two-electrode additive model, a full-cell linear EIS observation uniquely identifies the separate positive- and negative-electrode contributions.
claims.query_scope: the sum-versus-difference measurement structure described by the 2nd-NLEIS work; practical noise, broader circuit families, and general battery causality are outside the formal witness
assumptions: the linear full-cell observable is the sum of the two electrode contributions
the second-harmonic observable has opposite parity and is their difference
the scalar witness represents one frequency or one declared feature of the spectrum
both witness allocations are admissible in the scoped model class

evidence.role: hash-bound audit of 30 paired public EIS and second-harmonic spectra across ten conditions
Lean kernel receipt for the compensating-shift and parity-separation theorems
primary analytical theory for second-harmonic NLEIS
MIT-licensed public data and analysis release

countermodels.explanation: Both allocations give the same linear full-cell sum of 4, while their opposite-parity second-harmonic targets are 2 and 0.

empirical_decision.rule: support unique electrode allocation only if a frozen multistart and uncertainty analysis shows one practically unique allocation under model broadening
empirical_decision.evidence_summary: The public corpus contains 30 finite paired spectra and nonzero second-harmonic signals, but the independent fit and multistart reproduction has not yet been completed.

closure_measurements: measure the phase-resolved second-harmonic spectrum under the same state of charge and cell condition

closure_experiments.measured_variable: linear EIS plus phase-resolved second-harmonic NLEIS over the shared frequency range
closure_experiments.intervention_or_condition: fit the frozen two-electrode model to EIS alone and jointly to EIS plus NLEIS using identical multistart seeds and held-out frequencies

predictions.expected_outcome: linear sum equals 4 and second-harmonic difference equals 2
predictions.rationale: opposite parity preserves electrode-allocation information removed by the sum

predictions.expected_outcome: linear sum equals 4 and second-harmonic difference equals 0
predictions.rationale: equal electrode contributions cancel in the opposite-parity channel

closure_experiments.decision_rule: Declare practical closure only if the joint fit separates the prespecified witness classes on held-out second-harmonic frequencies and materially contracts the electrode-parameter confidence region relative to EIS alone.
closure_experiments.safety_or_ethics: standard moderate-amplitude electrochemical spectroscopy controls; verify linear-channel integrity and heating
